questions.question: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.note: Mercury is the only metallic element that is liquid at standard conditions; gallium and caesium melt just above room temperature.

questions.question: Which is the most abundant metal in the Earth's crust?
questions.note: Aluminium makes up about 8% of the Earth's crust, more than any other metal.

questions.question: Which metal has the highest electrical conductivity of all metals?
questions.note: Silver beats copper, which is the more common (and cheaper) conductor in wires.

questions.question: Bronze is traditionally an alloy of copper and which metal?
questions.note: Modern bronze is typically about 88% copper and 12% tin.

questions.question: Brass is an alloy of copper and which metal?
questions.note: The copper-to-zinc ratio is varied to get different colours and properties.

questions.question: When zinc reacts with dilute sulfuric acid, which gas is released?
questions.note: The acid strips zinc's protective layer and the reaction releases hydrogen gas.

questions.question: Which mineral is the main ore of iron?
questions.note: Hematite (Fe2O3) is the main ore of iron; bauxite is the ore of aluminium.

questions.question: Cast iron typically contains how much carbon?
questions.note: Cast iron has more than 2% carbon, which makes it hard but brittle; steel has less.

questions.question: Stainless steels contain a minimum of about how much chromium?
questions.note: At least about 10.5% chromium is needed to form the protective surface layer.

questions.question: In a blast furnace, what is the main role of coke?
questions.option_1: A flux that removes impurities from the melt
questions.option_2: A reducing agent for the iron ore
questions.option_4: A lining material for the furnace
questions.note: Coke (carbon) reduces the iron oxide to molten iron and also burns as fuel.

questions.question: In basic oxygen steelmaking, what is blown into molten pig iron to lower its carbon content?
questions.note: Pure oxygen blown through the melt burns off excess carbon, turning pig iron into steel.

questions.question: Wrought iron is best described as iron with what?
questions.note: Wrought iron has less than about 0.05% carbon plus fibrous slag, making it soft and easy to forge.

questions.question: The eutectoid temperature in the iron-carbon diagram is about?
questions.category: Inside steel: phases and heat treatment
questions.note: At 727 °C austenite of eutectoid composition transforms into pearlite.

questions.question: Pearlite has a lamellar structure made of alternating layers of?
questions.category: Inside steel: phases and heat treatment
questions.note: Pearlite is roughly 87% soft ferrite and 13% hard cementite in layers.

questions.question: The eutectoid composition of steel is about how much carbon?
questions.category: Inside steel: phases and heat treatment
questions.note: A steel with 0.76% carbon transforms entirely into pearlite at the eutectoid temperature.

questions.question: Martensite forms in carbon steels when austenite is?
questions.category: Inside steel: phases and heat treatment
questions.note: Quenching is so fast that carbon atoms cannot escape, trapping them in a hard, strained structure.

questions.question: Austenite (gamma iron) has which crystal structure?
questions.category: Inside steel: phases and heat treatment
questions.note: Above 912 °C iron switches from body-centered cubic to the face-centered cubic gamma form.

questions.question: Annealing is a heat treatment used mainly to?
questions.option_3: Add carbon to the surface by carburizing
questions.category: Inside steel: phases and heat treatment
questions.note: Annealing softens the metal and relieves internal stresses, making it more workable.

questions.question: In the Hall-Héroult process, alumina dissolved in molten cryolite is treated how to extract aluminium?
questions.note: Electric current through the molten bath deposits aluminium metal at the cathode.

questions.question: The Bayer process produces alumina from which ore?
questions.note: Bauxite is digested in hot caustic soda, leaving alumina that feeds the Hall-Héroult cells.

questions.question: The Kroll process is the main industrial method for producing which metal?
questions.note: Titanium tetrachloride is reduced with magnesium to give titanium sponge.

questions.question: Pure copper for electrical use is produced at the final stage by?
questions.note: Electrorefining deposits copper of about 99.99% purity at the cathode.

questions.question: Duralumin, one of the earliest age-hardenable alloys used in aircraft, is aluminium alloyed mainly with?
questions.note: Duralumin is a classic aluminium-copper alloy that gains strength as fine precipitates form.

questions.question: Galvanization protects steel or iron from rusting by coating it with?
questions.note: The zinc coating shields the steel and corrodes sacrificially in its place.

questions.question: The Charpy V-notch test measures what property of a material?
questions.note: A swinging pendulum breaks the notched sample; the energy it loses is the material's toughness.

questions.question: The ultimate tensile strength (UTS) is?
questions.option_1: The stress at which a material starts to deform permanently under load
questions.option_2: The stress at fracture under impact
questions.option_3: The maximum stress a material can withstand while being stretched
questions.option_4: The stress a material can bear forever
questions.note: UTS is the peak of the stress-strain curve, the highest load the material can take in tension.

questions.question: The Brinell hardness test presses what into the material's surface?
questions.note: A hard ball (usually tungsten carbide) is pushed in under a set load; the dent size gives the hardness.

questions.question: Fatigue failure in a material is caused by?
questions.note: Cracks start and grow under many load cycles, even at stresses below the ultimate strength.

questions.question: Creep is the tendency of a solid material to?
questions.option_1: Fracture suddenly without any applied load
questions.option_2: Deform slowly and permanently under stress
questions.note: Creep gets worse with time and temperature, which is why it matters in turbines and boilers.

questions.question: In a tensile test, ductility is commonly measured by?
questions.note: How much the sample stretches before breaking, in percent, tells how ductile it is.

questions.question: Rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen in the presence of?
questions.note: Rust is a mix of iron oxides and hydroxides that needs both oxygen and moisture to form.

questions.question: Sacrificial anodes protecting ship hulls and pipelines are commonly made of?
questions.note: These metals are more active than steel, so they corrode first and spare the structure.

questions.question: TIG (tungsten inert gas) welding uses which kind of electrode?
questions.note: The tungsten electrode does not melt; an inert gas shields the arc and the weld pool.

questions.question: Traditional solder used to join electronic components is a fusible alloy of?
questions.note: Classic solder melts at low temperature to bond metal parts without melting them.

questions.question: Carburizing hardens the surface of steel by making it absorb which element while heated?
questions.note: Heating steel in a carbon-rich medium diffuses carbon into the surface so it can be hardened.

questions.question: In galvanic corrosion of two different metals in contact, which metal corrodes preferentially?
questions.note: The more active metal becomes the anode of the galvanic cell and corrodes first.

questions.question: The iron pillar of Delhi is famous for what?
questions.category: Metallurgy in India and modern materials
questions.note: A protective film on its high-phosphorus iron has kept it nearly rust-free for centuries.

questions.question: Wootz steel, a high-carbon crucible steel once famous worldwide, originated in?
questions.category: Metallurgy in India and modern materials
questions.note: Wootz steel was made in ancient India from the mid-1st millennium BC and traded widely.

questions.question: Which country produced more than half of the world's steel in 2023?
questions.category: Metallurgy in India and modern materials
questions.note: China accounted for about 54% of world steel production in 2023.

questions.question: Nickel-based superalloys are the material of choice for which high-temperature application?
questions.option_2: Gas turbine blades in jet engines
questions.category: Metallurgy in India and modern materials
questions.note: They keep their strength near their melting point, ideal for hot turbine sections.

questions.question: Nitinol, the shape-memory alloy, is made of nickel and which other metal in roughly equal atomic percentages?
questions.category: Metallurgy in India and modern materials
questions.note: Nickel-titanium 'remembers' its shape and springs back when warmed.

questions.question: Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) was established in 1907 in which city?
questions.category: Metallurgy in India and modern materials
questions.note: The company was established on 26 August 1907 in Jamshedpur.

questions.question: Chalcopyrite is the main ore of which metal?
questions.note: Chalcopyrite (copper iron sulfide, CuFeS2) is the most abundant copper ore mineral.

questions.question: Cassiterite is the main ore of which metal?
questions.note: Cassiterite is tin oxide (SnO2) and remains the most important source of tin.

questions.question: Galena is the chief ore of which metal?
questions.note: Galena is lead sulfide (PbS) and is also an important source of silver.

questions.question: Cinnabar has long been mined as the main ore of which metal?
questions.note: Cinnabar is mercury sulfide (HgS); its bright red form was ground into the pigment vermilion.

questions.question: Magnetite, an important iron ore, has which chemical formula?
questions.note: Magnetite is ferrimagnetic, so it is naturally attracted to a magnet.

questions.question: Rutile is a major ore mineral of which metal?
questions.note: Rutile is titanium dioxide (TiO2), mined for white pigment as well as titanium metal.

questions.question: In a blast furnace, limestone is charged mainly to?
questions.option_1: Cool the gases leaving the furnace top
questions.option_2: Add extra heat as the charge burns
questions.option_3: Form a fluid slag with impurities
questions.option_4: Increase the carbon content of iron
questions.note: Limestone acts as a flux; it combines with silica and ash so the slag can be tapped off.

questions.question: Roasting an ore means heating it strongly in the presence of?
questions.note: During roasting the sulfide is converted to an oxide, often the step before smelting.

questions.question: The Bessemer process removed carbon from pig iron by blowing what through the melt?
questions.note: Blowing air through molten pig iron burns out carbon; it was the first inexpensive way to mass-produce steel.

questions.question: The Mond process extracts and purifies which metal using a volatile carbonyl compound?
questions.note: Carbon monoxide and nickel readily combine into a volatile complex that is decomposed back to deposit very pure nickel.

questions.question: In copper smelting, "matte" is a molten mixture mainly of?
questions.note: Matte goes to a final converting step, which produces blister copper.

questions.question: The name "pig iron" comes from?
questions.option_1: Its dirty grey colour right after casting
questions.option_2: Its traditional use in farm equipment
questions.option_3: The strong smell given off during casting
questions.option_4: Molds shaped like piglets by a sow
questions.note: The ingots branched off a central runner, resembling a litter of piglets nursing a sow.

questions.question: Stainless steel resists rust because of a thin, self-repairing surface layer of?
questions.note: The chromium in the steel forms a passive film that protects the metal and self-heals in air.

questions.question: High-speed steels stay hard even when red-hot mainly because they are alloyed with?
questions.note: They withstand higher temperatures without losing hardness, so cutting tools can run faster.

questions.question: Invar, used where almost zero thermal expansion is needed, is iron alloyed with about 36% of?
questions.note: The grade called Invar 36 is about 36% nickel and 64% iron.

questions.question: Electrical steels in transformer cores are alloyed with which element to cut energy losses?
questions.note: Adding silicon raises resistivity, which reduces eddy-current losses in the core.

questions.question: Weathering steels such as Cor-Ten are designed to?
questions.option_1: Stay shiny for decades with no coating
questions.option_2: Form a stable, protective rust layer
questions.option_3: Resist all corrosion, even in seawater
questions.option_4: Soften slowly on exposure to rain
questions.note: The adherent rust-like layer slows further attack, so bridges can be left unpainted.

questions.question: Manganese is added during steelmaking mainly to?
questions.option_1: Improve the surface polish of finished steel
questions.option_2: Raise the melting point of the steel bath
questions.option_3: Increase the magnetic response of the steel
questions.option_4: Fix sulfur and oxygen in harmless compounds
questions.note: Manganese is essential to steelmaking for its sulfur-fixing, deoxidizing and alloying properties.

questions.question: Work hardening (strain hardening) makes a metal?
questions.note: Bend a wire back and forth and it hardens where it bends, until it snaps.

questions.question: In a steel mill, "hot rolling" is rolling done?
questions.option_1: Underwater, so the surface cools fast
questions.option_3: Only after the steel is fully hardened
questions.note: Above the recrystallization temperature new grains form as the steel deforms, so it stays workable.

questions.question: In extrusion, metal is shaped by?
questions.option_1: Pushing it through a die opening
questions.option_2: Spinning it on a lathe at high speed
questions.option_4: Rolling it into thin wide sheets
questions.note: Extrusion makes long parts with a fixed cross-section, like aluminium window frames and tubes.

questions.question: Sintering in powder metallurgy bonds metal particles by?
questions.option_1: Melting them completely in a furnace
questions.option_2: Gluing them with a resin binder
questions.option_4: Dissolving them in a strong acid
questions.note: Atoms diffuse across the particle boundaries and fuse the compact without melting it.

questions.question: Forging can make a part stronger mainly because it?
questions.option_2: Refines the grain and follows the part's shape
questions.option_3: Coats the part with a protective slag layer
questions.option_4: Cools the part very slowly in still air
questions.note: Etched forged parts show grain flow that follows the shape, which helps carry the load.

questions.question: Wire drawing thins a metal rod by?
questions.option_1: Rolling it repeatedly between flat plates
questions.option_2: Stretching it under infrared heat lamps
questions.option_3: Squeezing it flat in a hydraulic press
questions.option_4: Pulling it through a series of dies
questions.note: Repeated draws, with anneals to soften the metal in between, take rod down to fine wire.

questions.question: Magnesium is chosen for aircraft parts and laptop bodies mainly because it is?
questions.note: Magnesium has about two-thirds the density of aluminium.

questions.question: The widely used titanium alloy Ti-6Al-4V contains titanium, aluminium and?
questions.note: Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5) is one of the most commonly used titanium alloys, with high strength and low density.

questions.question: Aluminium-lithium alloys are used in modern airliners mainly because they are?
questions.option_1: Easier to weld than standard aerospace steel
questions.option_2: Lighter and stiffer than older aluminium alloys
questions.option_4: Cheaper per kilogram than plain aluminium
questions.note: Each percent of lithium cuts density by about 3% and raises stiffness by about 5%.

questions.question: Monel, used in marine and chemical equipment, is an alloy of nickel mainly with?
questions.note: Monel is roughly two-thirds nickel and one-third copper and resists seawater well.

questions.question: Modern pewter, used for mugs and tableware, consists mostly of?
questions.note: Modern pewter replaces lead with antimony and copper; a typical mix is about 92% tin.

questions.question: Beryllium copper tools are chosen for work near flammable vapors because they?
questions.note: Beryllium copper is non-sparking, so it is used for tools in hazardous environments.

questions.question: Pitting corrosion is especially dangerous because it?
questions.option_1: Only attacks surfaces that are painted
questions.option_2: Bores small holes with little metal loss
questions.option_4: Occurs only in seawater or brines
questions.note: A few deep pits can perforate a pipe or tank that still looks almost untouched.

questions.question: Stress corrosion cracking happens when a susceptible alloy faces?
questions.option_1: High heat alone at service temperature
questions.option_2: Tensile stress plus a corrosive environment
questions.option_3: Vibration in perfectly dry, clean air
questions.option_4: Tensile stress in completely dry air
questions.note: Cracks can grow with little visible damage, leading to sudden failure.

questions.question: Crevice corrosion typically starts?
questions.option_1: On freely exposed and painted surfaces
questions.option_2: Only at very high service temperatures
questions.option_3: Under gaskets, deposits and lap joints
questions.note: Stagnant solution trapped in the crevice turns acidic and attacks the metal locally.

questions.question: Anodizing protects aluminium by?
questions.option_1: Painting it with an epoxy primer coat
questions.option_2: Plating it with a layer of zinc
questions.option_3: Dipping it in hot linseed oil
questions.note: The anodized layer is integral with the metal and can be dyed in colors.

questions.question: Cathodic protection keeps a buried steel pipeline from rusting by making the pipe the?
questions.note: It is done with a sacrificial metal or an impressed current system.

questions.question: Intergranular corrosion in sensitized stainless steel is caused by?
questions.option_3: Chromium carbides forming at the grain boundaries
questions.option_4: Excess nickel concentrated near the surface
questions.note: The carbides deplete chromium next to the grain boundaries, leaving paths for attack.

questions.question: The Bhilai Steel Plant was set up in the 1950s with the collaboration of which country?
questions.note: Bhilai, in Chhattisgarh, was established with Soviet collaboration and is India's first and main producer of steel rails.

questions.question: SAIL, India's largest government-owned steel producer, stands for?
questions.note: SAIL runs integrated steel plants at Bhilai, Bokaro, Rourkela, Durgapur and Burnpur.

questions.question: The Zawar mines in Rajasthan are known for ancient large-scale production of which metal?
questions.note: Zawar smelted zinc in retorts centuries before industrial zinc production in Europe.

questions.question: India is the world's largest producer of direct reduced iron, also called?
questions.note: Direct reduced iron is made by reducing iron ore below the melting point of iron.

questions.question: An electric arc furnace makes steel mainly by melting?
questions.note: Graphite electrodes strike an arc that melts the scrap charge for recycling into new steel.

questions.question: Continuous casting solidifies molten steel directly into?
questions.note: Continuous casting skips ingot casting and is used for nearly all steel today.
